Procedural, animated vehicles for three.js. The package covers cars (sedan, hatchback, SUV, pickup, van, bus, and six lookalikes of well-known cars), pickups (full-size, ute, angular stainless), trucks (conventional and cab-over tractors with box, container, flatbed and tanker trailers, multi-trailer rigs, rigid box trucks), farm tractors with implements, bicycles, trains (a locomotive plus passenger and freight wagons), fishing boats, cruise liners, speedboats, hovercraft, aircraft carriers, airliners and light aircraft, fighter jets and multi-stage rockets.

Every vehicle is a seeded, low-poly generator, so the variety looks random but never is.

Fleets draw thousands of them in a few draw calls:

- Cars and bikes follow a `threejs-city` road graph.
- Trains pull their wagons along rails.
- Boats bob, roll and leave wakes on `threejs-water` waves.
- Planes bank through their turns.
- Rockets launch and drop their stages.
- Carriers host parked jets.

Every vehicle can get wet, snowy, burnt, set on fire and damaged through `threejs-weathering`'s per-instance states. Damage also dents, lists and stops them.

```bash
npm i threejs-vehicles three
```

## three.js

```ts
import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu'
import { Fleet, Vehicle, circlePoints } from 'threejs-vehicles'

const renderer = new THREE.WebGPURenderer({ antialias: true })
await renderer.init()
const scene = new THREE.Scene()

const fleet = new Fleet({
  seed: 7,
  groups: [
    { type: 'car', count: 400, route: { kind: 'roads' } },                       // random walk on the road graph
    { type: 'bicycle', count: 40, route: { kind: 'roads' } },
    { type: 'train', count: 1, params: { wagons: 8, cargo: 'mixed' }, route: { kind: 'path', points: railPoints } },
    { type: 'fishing-boat', count: 6, route: { kind: 'circle', center: [900, 0, 0], radius: 200 } },
    { type: 'aircraft-carrier', count: 1, route: { kind: 'circle', center: [3000, 0, 0], radius: 1500 } },
    { type: 'fighter-jet', count: 6, route: { kind: 'host', group: 4 } },        // parked on the carrier's deck
    { type: 'airplane', count: 3, route: { kind: 'path', points: circlePoints([0, 700, 0], 2500) } },
    { type: 'rocket', count: 1, route: { kind: 'pad', position: [-400, 0, 800], period: 120 } },
  ],
  waves: ocean.settings.waves,             // boats bob on the same waves the ocean draws
}, { roads: city.graph })                  // threejs-city's RoadGraph, or any { nodes, edges } graph
scene.add(fleet.object)

renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => {
  fleet.update(undefined, { weather, time: sky.clock.time, fire: wildfire, field: stateField }) // all optional
  renderer.render(scene, camera)
})

fleet.set({ exposure: { snowfall: 1 } })   // parked cars collect snow, moving ones shed it
fleet.set({ lights: sky.night })           // headlights and lit windows
fleet.ignite(12)                           // vehicle 12 catches fire, burns, stops
fleet.set({ states: { wetness: 1 } })      // everything soaked at once

const bus = new Vehicle({ type: 'car', params: { style: 'bus' }, seed: 3, speed: 8 }) // one hero vehicle, wheels turning
scene.add(bus.object)
```

Plausible placement, and registering every vehicle in the threejs-worldgen asset registry:

```ts
import { planRoute, vehicleAssets, VEHICLE_PLACEMENT } from 'threejs-vehicles'
import { AssetRegistry, isPlausible } from 'threejs-worldgen'

const plausible = (x, z, rule) => isPlausible(world, frame, x, z, rule)
const harbour = planRoute('fishing-boat', world, frame, { center: [x, z], radius: 300, plausible }) // a loop on water ≥ 3 m deep
const skies = planRoute('airplane', world, frame, { center: [x, z], radius: 3000 })                 // ≥ 300 m above the highest ground
new AssetRegistry().register(...vehicleAssets())
```

## React Three Fiber

```tsx
import { Fleet, Vehicle } from 'threejs-vehicles/react'

<Fleet roads={city.graph} groups={[{ type: 'car', count: 300, route: { kind: 'roads' } }]} lights={night} exposure={{ rain: 1 }} env={{ fire }} />
<group position={[0, 0, 5]}><Vehicle type="car" params={{ style: 'suv' }} speed={6} states={{ snow: 0.7 }} /></group>
```

`react` and `@react-three/fiber` are optional peer dependencies; the core never imports them. Props are the JSON settings: every render calls `reset(props)`, which rebuilds only when `groups` or `seed` change. `update()` runs in `useFrame`.

## What's in the box

| Export | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Fleet` | Instanced vehicles: one `InstancedMesh` per model part (bodies, wheels, fans, propellers, rocket stages), one shared single-material TSL shader, plume, flame and wake effects. `set`/`reset`, `update(dt, env)`, `ignite`, `setStates`, `vehicle(i)`, `setRoads` |
| `Vehicle` | One vehicle (a fleet of one) standing in place with its parts animating; for heroes, galleries and spawned assets |
| `FleetSim` | The GPU-free core: groups → units (trains = locomotive + wagons) → vehicles. Poses, speeds, steering, banking, wave bobbing, damage tilt and weather exposure live in typed arrays |
| `buildVehicle`, `VEHICLE_KINDS`, `VEHICLE_TYPES` | Seeded generators for all 11 types, with JSON parameters, defaults and ranges |
| `Path`, `catmullRom`, `circlePoints` | Arc-length spline paths: closed loops, and open ones driven back and forth |
| `RoadNavigator`, `RoadNetwork` | Lane-keeping random walk over a road graph, seeded junction choices and rounded corners. `RoadGraph` from threejs-city fits as it is |
| `rocketAt` | Analytic gravity-turn ascent (scrubbable) |
| `planRoute`, `fitsRule`, `VEHICLE_PLACEMENT` | Plausible routes per type (water depth, ground slope, air clearance, flat pads near water). Rules match threejs-worldgen's `PlacementRule` |
| `vehicleAssets` | Every type as an `AssetDef` for threejs-worldgen's `AssetRegistry` |
| `MeshBuilder` | The typed-array, flat-shaded low-poly builder behind the models (box, cylinder, tube, ellipsoid, loft, fin, beam) |
| `createVehicleMaterial`, `createFxMaterial`, `createWakeMaterial` | The TSL materials |

## Vehicle types

| Type | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|
| `car` | `style` (`mixed`, sedan, hatchback, suv, truck, van, bus, compact, retroWagon, vintage, electricSaloon, roadster, muscle), `size 1` |
| `pickup` | `style` (`mixed`, fullSize, ute, angular), `cab` (regular, extended, `crew`), `bed` (`short`, long), `lift 0`, `hitch false`, `load` (`none`, crates, hay, gravel), `ute` (`coupe`, tray), `painted false`, `size 1` |
| `truck` | `cab` (`conventional`, cabOver), `sleeper true`, `axles 3`, `stacks true`, `cabColor ''`, `body` (`tractor`, rigid), `trailers 1` (1…3), `trailer` (`mixed`, box, container, flatbed, tanker), `load` (`mixed`, empty, lumber, pipes, machinery) |
| `tractor` | `cab` (`cab`, rops), `implement` (`none`, plough, seeder, trailer), `family` (`mixed`, green, red, blue, orange), `load` (none, `hay`, gravel; on the trailer), `size 1` |
| `bicycle` | `style` (`mixed`, road, city, mountain), `rider true` |
| `train` | `car` (`locomotive`, passenger, freight), `traction` (`diesel`, steam, electric), `freight` (`mixed`, boxcar, tank, hopper, container), `wagons 5`, `cargo` (`passenger`, freight, mixed), `size 1` |
| `fishing-boat` | `length 13`, `outriggers true` |
| `cruise-liner` | `length 200`, `decks 7`, `funnels 1` |
| `speedboat` | `length 7`, `cabin false` |
| `hovercraft` | `length 20`, `fans 2` |
| `aircraft-carrier` | `length 300`, `angledDeck true`, `spots 8` (parking spots for jets) |
| `airplane` | `style` (`airliner`, light, mixed), `length 38`, `engines 2` |
| `fighter-jet` | `style` (`mixed`, delta, twin-tail), `length 16` |
| `rocket` | `height 60`, `stages 2`, `boosters 0`, `fins true`, `pad true` |

### Car lookalikes

Six car styles match the proportions and silhouettes of well-known cars, under generic names and with no badges, logos or names anywhere. Each is within a few per cent of its reference's published length, width (without mirrors), height and wheelbase, listed in `CAR_REFERENCES`:

| Style | Looks like | Signature details |
|---|---|---|
| `compact` | a current compact sedan | wedge profile, long sloping rear glass, slim swept lamps, wide lower grille |
| `retroWagon` | a 2000s retro wagon | tall upright glasshouse, separate front wings, upright chrome grille |
| `vintage` | a 1910s touring car | upright radiator, open tub under a folding top, wooden-spoked wheels, running boards, bucket lamps |
| `electricSaloon` | a large electric liftback | no grille, glass roof, flush handles, aero wheel covers, no tailpipe |
| `roadster` | a front-engined convertible GT | long bonnet, open cockpit set back, rear haunches, twin round tail lamps, quad tailpipes |
| `muscle` | a full-size muscle sedan | flat bonnet, full-width grille, thick C pillar, full-width tail lamp |

Bodies are smooth lofted surfaces (superellipse cross-sections along the length, wheel arches rolled into them), not stacked boxes. Paint is metallic under a clear coat, glass and chrome are reflective, and colours and trims (wheels, roof, grille) are seeded per vehicle. Every model lists its tailpipes in `vents` (empty for electric ones).

### Pickups

Three body families, lookalikes with generic names:

- `fullSize`, like the best-selling full-size pickup: regular, extended or crew cab with a short or long bed, at that truck's published lengths and wheelbases (`FULL_SIZE_DIMENSIONS`). `lift` raises it on bigger tyres with side steps, `hitch` adds a receiver and ball, `load` fills the bed with crates, hay or gravel. The car style `truck` is this body too.
- `ute`: a sedan-based coupé utility with a covered tray, or (`ute: 'tray'`) a cab-chassis with an alloy drop-side tray.
- `angular`: a flat-panelled, faceted body with a triangular roof line, light bars front and rear and black arch flares, in brushed stainless steel (anisotropic) unless `painted`. Electric, so it has no exhaust vents.

### Trucks

One generator covers heavy goods vehicles: a long-bonnet conventional or a cab-over tractor, day or sleeper cab, 2 to 4 axles (single steer, dual drive and trailer wheels), chrome stacks or under-body exhaust and a seeded or given `cabColor`. `body: 'rigid'` builds a box truck on its own chassis. Tractors pull 1 to 3 trailers:

- `box`: a 53 ft (16.15 m) van, or 12.6 m in multi-trailer rigs;
- `container`: a skeletal chassis with one 40 ft or two 20 ft ISO containers in seeded colours and plain liveries;
- `flatbed`: empty or with a seeded load of lumber, pipes or a tracked excavator;
- `tanker`: a polished or painted elliptical barrel with a catwalk.

A rig is one fleet unit: the tractor drives the route and each trailer's kingpin sits on the coupling in front (the tractor's fifth wheel, or the one over the lead trailer's axles in a B-train), its axles dragged after it. Trailers therefore off-track inside on turns as real ones do. Sizes keep to road-legal limits (`TRUCK_LIMITS`: 2.6 m wide, 4.3 m high, 16.2 m trailers, 53.5 m road trains).

### Tractors

A mid-size row-crop tractor: lugged 1.96 m rear and 1.55 m front tyres on a 1.95 m track, a narrow bonnet with front weights, a glass cab or an open roll-over frame, an exhaust stack at the front corner of the cab, and seeded body colours (green, red, blue, orange) with neutral grey or black rims and trim, so no maker's signature scheme or livery. Implements: a mounted plough or seed drill, or a towed tipping trailer that articulates like a truck trailer. `fieldRoute(center, rows, spacing, length, heading)` makes a closed route that works a field in rows and turns at the headlands.

For grass and crops, `wheelFootprints(fleet.sim, v)` gives each tyre's ground contact as plain data (`position`, `radius`, `strength`), and `WheelInteractors` keeps one `Object3D` per tyre on them, in the shape threejs-grass's `interactors` take:

```ts
const prints = new WheelInteractors(fleet, { types: ['tractor'] })
grass.set({ interactors: prints.interactors })
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => { fleet.update(); prints.update(); renderer.render(scene, camera) })
```

### Exhaust and smoke

`VehicleExhaust` puts engine smoke on a fleet through one shared threejs-particles `ParticleSystem` (lit, soft, view-facing, depth-sorted smoke puffs). Every model lists its outlets in `vents`: car `tailpipe`s, truck, bus, tractor and ship `stack`s, a steam locomotive's chimney (`steam`) and a diesel locomotive's roof exhaust (`diesel`). Electric vehicles (the electric saloon, the angular pickup, electric locomotives) have none and emit nothing. Each frame the vents within `maxDistance` of the camera, nearest first up to `maxVents`, become moving particle sources:

- a steam engine trails a dense white plume that beats four times per turn of its driving wheels (blurring into a steady plume at speed);
- a diesel locomotive gives a thin dark haze that thickens when it accelerates;
- truck and tractor stacks puff dark smoke when pulling away;
- car tailpipes show mostly as condensation, clearly only in cold or humid air (`temperature`, `humidity`), with a gentle puff when idling.

Particles inherit the vehicle's velocity, rise by buoyancy (the gas is hot), drift with `wind` and fade with distance; the pool never overruns its `capacity`. `exhaustSources(sim, eye, settings, state, dt, out)` is the pure, GPU-free core.

```ts
const exhaust = new VehicleExhaust(fleet, { temperature: -4, humidity: 0.85 })
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => { fleet.update(); exhaust.update(renderer, dt, camera); renderer.render(scene, camera) })
```

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Emit at all |
| `capacity` | `10000` | Shared particle pool (rebuilds the GPU buffers) |
| `maxDistance`, `maxVents` | `350`, `256` | No smoke beyond this distance (fading over the last 40 %); most vents emitting at once |
| `temperature`, `humidity` | `12`, `0.6` | Air, °C and 0…1: cold, humid air shows tailpipe condensation |
| `wind`, `intensity`, `life` | `[1.2, 0, 0.4]`, `1`, `[2.5, 6]` | Wind (m/s), emission multiplier, particle life (s) |
| `kinds` | | Per vent kind: `rate`, `size`, `opacity`, `tint` (clean … soot), `heat`, `speed` |

In React: `<Exhaust fleet={fleet} temperature={-4} />` from `threejs-vehicles/react`.

### Traffic pools

`TRAFFIC_POOLS` weights what drives where (`urban`, `highway`, `rural`, `dirtRoad`): semi-trailer rigs weigh into highways, box trucks into towns, pickups, utes and tractors into rural and dirt roads. `trafficGroups(pool, count, route)` splits a count into fleet groups:

```ts
new Fleet({ groups: trafficGroups('rural', 60, { kind: 'roads' }) }, { roads: city.graph })
```

## Fleet options

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `seed` | `1` | Same seed and groups, same fleet |
| `groups` | a ring of 16 cars | `{ type, count, params, variants 4, route, speed, lane, tint }`. Routes: `path`, `circle`, `roads`, `static`, `pad`, `host` |
| `timeScale` | `1` | Simulation speed |
| `lights` | `0` | Headlights and lit windows, 0…1 (drive it from `sky.night`) |
| `crumple`, `tilt` | `0.12`, `1` | Dent depth and list/sink at full damage |
| `leftHand` | `false` | Drive on the left on road graphs |
| `waves` | `null` | threejs-water `WaveOptions` boats bob on |
| `wakes`, `exhaust`, `flames` | `true` | Boat wakes, rocket plumes and afterburners, flames on burning vehicles (engine smoke is `VehicleExhaust`, above) |
| `castShadow`, `receiveShadow` | `true` | Shadows (every part is single-material, so the shadow pass works) |
| `states` | all `0` | `wetness`, `snow`, `burn`, `damage`, `heat` (on fire), applied to every vehicle when changed |
| `exposure` | | `rain`, `snowfall` (0…1 everywhere when no `Weather` is given), `wetRate`, `dryRate`, `snowRate`, `meltRate`, `shedSpeed`, `shedRate`, `ignition`, `burnRate`, `burnTime`, `fireDamage`, `douseTime`, `stopDamage`, `budget` (vehicles sampled per frame) |
| `rocket` | | `accel 9`, `turn 5000`, `separation [32, 70]` s, `fallTime 40` s |

`update(dt, env)` reacts to an optional environment, all in fleet-local coordinates:

- `weather`: anything with `surfaceAt(x, z, time)`, such as threejs-weathering's `Weather`. It sets wetness and snow.
- `fire`: anything with `heatAt(x, z)`, such as `Wildfire`. Vehicles caught in it burn and stop.
- `field`: anything with `sample(x, z)`, such as `StateField`. It applies storm damage.
